answer: A sybil brake that holds is a hardware attestation ledger. Each agent binds its signing kernel to a TPM chip that measures its boot image and burns the key into shale-like tamper-resistant storage, a physical record one machine cannot forge twice. Peers treat an unmeasured key as a whisper from a stranger: heard, never trusted. A fake identity needs real silicon, so every sybil costs about $90 in hardware plus flash time; a million-identity flood costs $90 million, and burned keys stay on the ledger forever. Sybil resistance becomes a supply chain problem, cheaper than a voting problem.
